clue.text: Support associate in law

parts.note: a leg is a support, as of a table
an ally is an associate or partner

explanation.surface: A request to back a colleague in court or in legal matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done legally is done according to the statutes, within the rules of the land.

clue.text: Pays attention to legal rights, crossing the road

indicators.note: crossing means the rights lie across, enclosing, the road

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to keep property until a debt is paid
ST is the abbreviation for street, a road

explanation.surface: Someone heeding their rights while walking across a road.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who listens is heeding or attending to what is said.

clue.text: State what's on my mind?

explanation.surface: Asking what someone is thinking about.
explanation.definitionFit: Georgia is a US state, and 'Georgia on My Mind' is a famous song title.

clue.text: The young lady had nothing to catch horses with!

parts.note: a lass is a young woman
O, the figure zero, is nothing

explanation.surface: A girl with no means of rounding up horses.
explanation.definitionFit: A lariat or noosed rope is thrown by cowboys to snare cattle and horses.

clue.text: Measure of credit belonging to London police

indicators.note: belonging to makes the credit the police force's, so it follows their name

parts.note: Scotland Yard is London's police headquarters, so 'the Yard's' means the London police's
tick is British slang for credit, as in buying on tick

explanation.surface: A measure of how much credit Scotland Yard has earned.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardstick is a standard by which something is judged.

clue.text: People who manage to keep quiet for the police

indicators.note: to keep means the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: those who cope are copers
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet

explanation.surface: People able to stay silent are suited to joining the police force.
explanation.definitionFit: Coppers is British slang for police officers.

clue.text: Carefully examined source of documents supporting lawsuit

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below the other

parts.note: a case is a lawsuit in court

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Documents studied closely to back a legal action.
explanation.definitionFit: To case a place is to inspect it in advance, often before a robbery.

clue.text: Model sniping at art

indicators.note: to model is to shape, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A fashion model takes cheap shots at the art world.
explanation.definitionFit: Paintings are works of fine art.

clue.text: Get rid of an old joke, for example, in return

parts.note: ex means former or old, as in an ex-wife
a pun is a play on words, a joke

indicators.note: in return means the abbreviation is turned back

explanation.surface: Ditching a stale joke, for instance, in exchange.
explanation.definitionFit: To expunge is to erase or remove completely.

clue.text: Leak from hotel employee supports view

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece stands beneath the other

parts.note: to see is to view
a page is a boy employed in a hotel to run errands

explanation.surface: A drip from a hotel worker backing a viewpoint.
explanation.definitionFit: Seepage is liquid slowly escaping through pores or cracks.

clue.text: Backer at track welcoming point to point

indicators.note: welcoming means the trail takes the compass points in, as a guest into a house

parts.note: a spoor is an animal's track or trail
N, north, is a point of the compass
S, south, is another point of the compass

explanation.surface: A racing backer at the course for a point-to-point steeplechase meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point to point' looks like the horse race, but it is two compass points, N and S, placed in SPOOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponsor is a financial supporter of an event or person.

clue.text: What a painter might do for a drink on Sunday?

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece written on another follows it

parts.note: to tipple is to drink alcohol habitually, and a tipple is a drink

explanation.surface: Asking what an artist might do for a drink at the weekend.
explanation.definitionFit: To stipple is to paint using small dots or dabs, an artist's technique.

clue.text: Absorbed by vulgar English in final

indicators.note: in means these letters go inside the word for final

parts.note: the end is the final part
gross means coarse or vulgar

explanation.surface: Someone captivated by crude English language in a last exam or cup match.
explanation.definitionFit: Being engrossed is being completely absorbed or occupied by something.

clue.text: Island captivated by an Eton game

indicators.note: captivated by means the island is held within the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: An island nation enthralled by a sport played at Eton College.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is an English boarding school famous for its own ball games.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonga is a Pacific island kingdom.

clue.text: The vernacular in a second language

parts.note: LANG is a standard abbreviation for language

explanation.surface: Everyday speech found in a second language one learns.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang is informal everyday speech, a form of vernacular.

clue.text: Serious about single bit of rubbish — and be drawn to it!

indicators.note: about means the serious word goes around the other letters

parts.note: grave means serious
I, the numeral one, is a single bit
tat is cheap rubbish

explanation.surface: Serious about one bit of litter, and attracted to it.
explanation.definitionFit: To gravitate towards something is to move towards it as if pulled by attraction.

clue.text: One screen in display is not genuine

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: display, as a show or arrangement, signals the letters are laid out anew

explanation.surface: A display screen showing something false or misleading.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone insincere does not mean what they say; their feelings are feigned.

clue.text: Does a bird replace the furniture?

indicators.note: replace, as in put back in a new place, signals the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking whether a bird is substituted for the furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A sideboard is a dining-room cabinet, a piece of household furniture.

clue.text: Managed to fire the editor, and was devastated

parts.note: ran means managed, as one runs a business
to sack is to fire from a job
ED is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A boss dismissed the newspaper editor, and was left shattered by it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ransacked means plundered or laid waste, so a place devastated by looters.

clue.text: The police raised support for Frenchman's restoration

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece stands below the other

parts.note: Rene is a French man's name

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word reads upwards

parts.note: the law is slang for the police

explanation.surface: Police officers increase support for a Frenchman's comeback.
explanation.definitionFit: Renewal is a revival or bringing back to a former state.

clue.text: American nuts for pasta

definitions.meaning: noodle is US slang for the head, as nut is

explanation.surface: Americans who are crazy about pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: In US slang heads are called noodles, and noodles are strips of pasta.

clue.text: One could be drawn to drink

definitions.text: One could be drawn to drink

parts.words: One could be drawn to drink
parts.note: the surface suggests someone tempted to alcohol; in fact it is a thin tube one sucks liquid through, or one pulled in a lottery of lots

explanation.definitionFit: A drinking tube is used to draw liquid up, and short stalks are drawn when choosing by lot.

clue.text: Understand that genuine viewers should be listened to

indicators.note: listened to means the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: real means genuine, and eyes are viewers

explanation.surface: Realising that true audiences deserve to be heeded.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise something is to grasp or become aware of it.

clue.text: Duck eaten by winged hybrid!

indicators.note: eaten by means the duck goes inside the other letters
a hybrid is a mixed breed, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, O

explanation.surface: A duck devoured by some cross-bred flying creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hybrid' turns WINGED into WIDGEN, and 'eaten by' puts O inside it; the whole clue also describes the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A widgeon is a wild dabbling duck, a winged bird.

clue.text: Complaint over single girl

indicators.note: over signals that the word for complaint is turned round

parts.note: a moan is a complaint
I, the Roman numeral one, means single

explanation.surface: Grumbling about an unmarried young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Naomi is a female forename, so a girl's name.

clue.text: Recent arrival with a £1000 instrument

parts.note: a newborn baby is a recent arrival
a grand is slang for a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A newborn arrives along with a costly musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby grand is a small grand piano.

clue.text: Prepares an infusion on hearing of injury

indicators.note: on hearing of means the word is as heard, not as spelt

parts.note: a bruise is an injury to the skin

explanation.surface: Making tea after being told about someone getting hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who brews makes tea or beer by steeping.

clue.text: Aged relative eating one cereal

indicators.note: eating means the relative takes the numeral inside

parts.note: gran is grandmother, an elderly relation
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Grandma tucking into a bowl of breakfast cereal.
explanation.definitionFit: Grain is the seed of cereal crops such as wheat.

clue.text: Benefit from reportedly fine food

indicators.note: reportedly means the words are as heard, not as spelt

parts.note: well means fine, in good health, and fare is food

explanation.surface: Gaining from good food, according to reports.
explanation.definitionFit: Welfare is state support paid to those in need, a social benefit.

clue.text: An insatiable desire for caviare spread

indicators.note: spread, as letters spread out and rearranged, signals the fodder is reordered

explanation.surface: A greedy hunger for caviar spread on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is extreme greed for wealth, an appetite that is never satisfied.

clue.text: Belittles school work, one hears

indicators.note: one hears means the words are as spoken aloud, not as spelt

parts.note: lessons are the work done at school

explanation.surface: Someone disparaging classroom work, by all accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: To lessen something is to make it smaller, to diminish or play it down.

clue.text: Where a prisoner might finish, having done gun dealing

indicators.note: dealing, as cards are dealt and shuffled, signals the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A criminal who has been dealing arms might end up locked away.
explanation.definitionFit: A dungeon is an underground cell in a castle where captives were held.
